page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The big cheese
title: The big cheese
topic: Language for booking a hotel room
description:
Tip Top Trading have a serious issue to deal with - the arrival of the big boss from America, Mr Socrates. He is a particularly fussy man but because of his importance he gets his own way, including the type of hotel room he stays in. This is something that Anna will find out when she has to book his room.
This episode focuses on phrases to use when booking a hotel room.
phrases: Hello, I'd to check availability and prices for a room please.
Are there any business facilities such as internet and wi-fi?
I'd like to go ahead and make the reservation please.

listening_challenge.question:
How much is the nightly rate for the hotel?
£100.
listening_challenge.answer:
How much is the nightly rate for the hotel?
£100.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. Things haven't been going well at Tip Top Trading. There was a fire in the warehouse, caused by Mr Ingle's cigarette and now Mr Socrates – the big boss from America – has turned up unexpectedly.

transcript.speaker: Mr S
transcript.text: So honey, are you…?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Anna. I'm Anna, I work here as a sales executive. We haven't met before.

transcript.speaker: Mr S
transcript.text: We sure ain't. Looks like I've arrived just in the nick of time.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: (Out of breath)… what's going on… oh, Mr Socrates! Golly gosh, what an unexpected...

transcript.speaker: Mr S
transcript.text: Unexpected alright. Looks like this company is in a mess.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Err yes. It was OK when I popped out for some biscuits… erm, would you like one?

transcript.speaker: Mr S
transcript.text: Biscuits?! They're cookies man. Look, now what do I have to do to get a triple-shot, organic, skinny cappuccino round here?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'll get you one Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Mr S
transcript.text: It's OK honey. I need you to book me a hotel room. You... what's your name again…Paul… can you fetch me one?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Right Anna. Booking a room for Mr Socrates. This is something you can't get wrong.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well I've never done it before.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
I'm sure you'll be OK. When you book a room, here's what you could say:
Hello, I'd like to check availability and prices for a room please.
Does the price include breakfast?
Are there any business facilities such as internet and wi-fi?
I'd like to go ahead and make the reservation please.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK I'll give it a try. But where shall I look?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Try searching on the internet. Look for a five-star hotel. He is a five-star guest after all. Good luck.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. I better get back to the office and get started.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hi Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi Tom. Well done for saving Mr Ingle in that fire. You were very brave.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It was nothing really. So… err... what are you doing?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I've got to book a hotel for Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No! You know, we must be in trouble. He never visits.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Really? So where shall I book him in to?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well my friend runs a fantastic hotel – it's five star! It's called the Royal Imperial. Look, I've got his number. Give him a call, mention my name. You're bound to get a special rate.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks Tom.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No problem. Oh but don't forget, I've heard Mr S only likes a room with a single bed in it. He gets spooked out if there's another empty bed.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. OK, I might as well give it a try.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Hello. Royal Imperial Hotel.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, hello. I'd like to check availability and rates for a room.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: When for?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: For three nights from tonight. Your best room please!

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: All our rooms are the best! But… yes, we have one. It's £100 a night.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. I work with Tom…Tom Darcy… his friend runs the hotel. I wondered if you could offer me a special rate?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Tom Darcy? No I've never heard of him. Sorry, it's still £100.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Does the price include breakfast?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Yes. We offer a full continental breakfast of toast, or bread, oh, and tea…or coffee….and cereal.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh. And do you have any business facilities?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Well, we've got paper and pens.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I was thinking, internet, wi-fi… shoe-shine?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Yes. We've got that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Good. And most importantly, is this a single room?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: We've only got twin rooms.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Twins? You've only got room for twins?

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: No. We could take a bed out and just leave one in, if you want?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh that would be perfect. In that case, I'd like to go ahead and make a reservation please.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Good. How would you like to pay?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Well done Anna for booking the hotel but I have a feeling Tom's recommendation may not be as luxurious as he says. Let's hear the phrases Anna used when booking a hotel:
Hello, I'd like to check availability and prices for a room please.
Does the price include breakfast?
Are there any business facilities such as internet and wi-fi?
I'd like to go ahead and make the reservation please.
So the room is booked. I wonder what Mr Socrates will think of it? He's a particularly fussy man as we'll find out next time. Bye!
